chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from some of them, from Abu al-Maghra', from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him: 'A slave man had a free woman under his ownership, and he accused her [of adultery].' He said: 'What do the people of Kufa say regarding her?' I said: 'They say she is flogged.' He said: 'No, but he performs li'an with her just as he performs li'an with a free woman, and he confirms what we have said regarding the establishment of li'an between them.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling of li'an between a male slave and a free female slave?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *al-Istibsar*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) refutes the prevailing opinion of the people of Kufa, who held that a slave man accused of adultery with a free woman should merely be flogged. Instead, he establishes that the full ritual of *li'an* (mutual imprecation) applies equally to the slave, thereby confirming the consistency of legal procedures across different social strata in Shia jurisprudence. This ruling underscores the principle that the status of the slave does not diminish the procedural rights and obligations regarding marital accusations.
